Algebra 2 | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Linear Systems and Matrices

The Race Team’s Shopping List

Three unknowns, three clues

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 10–11
Topic
Three-Variable Systems
Standards
HSA-REI.C.6, HSA-CED.A.3, HSA-REI.C.8

Students reduce systems of three linear equations to two variables, solve them, check the solution in all three equations, and model a race team’s spending with three unknown prices.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Reduce a three-variable system to a two-variable system by elimination.
  • Solve a three-variable linear system and check the solution.
  • Model a real situation with three unknowns.
  • Recognise systems with no solution or infinitely many.

3Essential question

How many clues do you need to find three unknown prices, and how do you combine them?

5MTB connection

A race team buys spares in mixed orders, and the receipts show only totals. Three different orders are three equations: enough to work out each price.

Coaches use the same idea to split a training budget across three kinds of session, or to find three unknown average speeds from three timed loops.

The mathOn the trail
Three unknownsPrices of tubes, tires and grips
Three equationsThree different receipts
Ordered tripleThe price list
Inconsistent systemReceipts that can’t all be right

7MTB activity

MTB Problem-Based Exercise

Crack the Race-Team Receipts

Find three unknown prices from three receipts, then design receipts for a partner to crack.

You’ll need: The receipts (in the worked example); Calculator

The full lesson plan is for teachers

Teachers also get the mathematical foundation with worked examples, a 5-stage teaching plan with timings, step-by-step activity instructions, 4 guided examples with solutions, 9 practice problems, a 4-question exit ticket, a printable worksheet, common misconceptions, differentiation ideas and the complete answer key.
